passage:
A teacher showed students an old version of a popular website from many years ago. The design looked simple and strange, but students were interested.
They compared old pages with current ones. The internet, which felt modern and temporary, suddenly had history.
The teacher explained that websites can disappear quickly. Saving digital pages helps future people understand how ideas, businesses, and culture changed.
Students then saved screenshots of their school website and wrote descriptions for a class archive.
They learned that digital life is not automatically permanent. If people want future readers to understand today's online world, someone must save it before links break and pages vanish.
